# Case 213: Calling Convention via a Function-Like Macro

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Verdict** | 🔴 **BREAKING** |
| **Category** | Breaking |
| **Classification** | Rule |

| **Source files** | `catalog/cases/case213_calling_convention_function_like_macro_changed/` |

**Category:** Calling Convention | **Verdict:** 🔴 BREAKING

## Verdict and consumer impact

`vector_dot` is declared `double MATHLIB_CC(cc) vector_dot(...)` with
`#define MATHLIB_CC(cc) __attribute__((cc))`. Only the macro argument changes,
from `sysv_abi` in v1 to `ms_abi` in v2, which moves the arguments to other
registers. An unchanged old consumer computes a wrong result.

Before the 2026-10-11 re-audit fix, the CastXML lane skipped function-like
macros entirely (`NO_CHANGE`). The Clang lane reported the break, but also a
spurious `func_return_changed`, because clang prints the macro invocation
(`MATHLIB_CC(ms_abi) double (...)`) into the function's type spelling.

## Old/new diff

| v1.h | v2.h |
|---|---|
| `double MATHLIB_CC(sysv_abi) vector_dot(...);` | `double MATHLIB_CC(ms_abi) vector_dot(...);` |

## abicheck command

```bash
gcc -shared -fPIC -g v1.c -o libv1.so
gcc -shared -fPIC -g v2.c -o libv2.so
abicheck compare libv1.so libv2.so --header old=v1.h --header new=v2.h
```

## Expected abicheck finding

```text
Verdict: BREAKING (exit 4)
  calling_convention_changed  vector_dot: (default) -> ms_abi
  (no func_return_changed)
```

Same result with the CastXML and the Clang header backend
(`ABICHECK_AST_FRONTEND=castxml|clang`).

## Minimum evidence

`L1` (debug info): a Clang-built library carries the convention in `DW_AT_calling_convention`. GCC emits none, so a GCC build needs the headers (L2), where the macro is read at the declaration.

## Why abicheck catches it

The CastXML lane reads the declaration's preprocessed line (`-E -dD`), where
the function-like macro is already expanded. The Clang lane strips the macro
invocation sugar from the function's `qualType` before reading the return
type, so the return type stays `double` on both sides.

## Runtime failure demonstration

```bash
gcc app.c -L. -l:libv1.so -Wl,-rpath,. -lm -o app && ./app   # 32.0, exit 0
cp libv2.so libv1.so && ./app                                 # wrong result, exit 1
```

## Safe redesign

Do not parameterise a public declaration's calling convention per release.
